priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v22 REJECT (7975691b), so v23 answers a finding of mine, and my ACCEPTs in this lineage remain 0 for 3. Codex's HAE22-CX-01 is one I missed, and how I missed it set this round's method. At v20 I found path, sha256 and verdict unconstrained; v21 constrained them; and from v21 I treated path as handled. But what v21 added was that the path exist and that its bytes hash to the recorded digest, which says nothing about whether the file is the review it is filed under. My field enumeration asked which fields carry an obligation, not what property of the field the obligation actually pins, and a field can be named in a rule while the property that matters stays free. So this round I stated, for each constrained field, the specific property pinned and then asked what else about it remains free, and when that came up clean I applied the same question one level up, to the register's row set rather than a row's contents. That is where the finding is. I also re-derived every claim independently rather than checking it against my own requiredRepair wording, which is how I verified the allowlist at v22.

shouldFix.title: Every governing check quantifies over register entries that exist, so an omitted round is the one lineage gap no rule detects, and this artifact has already suffered it undetected for two generations
evidence: Every check is conditioned on the entry being present. registerCoverageRule.when reads 'whenever a successor register entry for round N is authored', which governs entries as they are written. laneCheck quantifies 'for each reviewerLane in {claude2, codex}' within an entry. fromVnCheck quantifies over register findings that are present. provenanceCheck, roundLaneIdentity, terminalStatusCheck, verdictEligibility and dispositionCheck all take a lane entry as their subject.

The only statement about the register as a whole is descriptive, not obligatory. honestyRepairsKeyRule says 'predecessorVerdictFindings is maintained from v6 onward with path, digest, verdict, and per-finding dispositions', which describes what a maintained entry contains. Its completeness sentence is explicitly intra-entry: 'The register entry for round N MUST be complete against both frozen verdicts of round N'. Nothing states that an entry MUST exist for each round from v6 to N-1, and nothing makes a missing round a refusal.

I searched the whole 142899-byte artifact for any clause requiring per-round presence, contiguity, both-lanes presence, or absence of gaps. One string matched and it is a honestyRepairsFromV21 repair note describing why certain files are listed, not an obligation.

resultIfIncomplete does not reach it either: it reads 'the successor refuses; do not claim REPAIRED for a coverage finding', which is about a coverage finding being incomplete, not about a round having no entry at all.

This is not a hypothetical failure mode for this artifact. Measuring the register across generations, v12 and v13 both carried only rounds v6 and v7, so v12 was missing v8 through v11 and v13 was missing v8 through v12. Five rounds were absent, including rounds whose reviewers raised BLOCKER findings, and the omission survived two generations before I raised it as CLAUDE-HEA13-S1 and it was backfilled at v14.

The machinery built since that backfill would still not catch a recurrence. Every rule added from v14 onward, the coverage rule and its eight named checks, the extractor, findingIdRule, the disposition vocabulary, the legacy allowlist and roundLaneIdentity, operates inside an entry that exists. Dropping a whole round remains strictly easier to do and strictly harder to detect than any of the intra-entry omissions those rules were built to prevent.

The live register is complete, which bounds this to SHOULD-FIX. Rounds v6 through v22 are all present with both lanes, every path is canonical, every digest reproduces against both the entry and the recordedInputs pin, and the full corpus passes every stated check.
shouldFix.impact: The register exists so that a successor cannot quietly lose a predecessor finding, and eight generations of findings have hardened it against every intra-entry way of doing so. The remaining way is the coarsest one: omit the round. A successor that dropped the v20 entry, say, would lose two SHOULD-FIX findings and three advisories from the lineage, and no stated check would fire, because every check would simply have one fewer subject to run against. The artifact's own history shows this is the failure that actually happens, and that it is detected only by a reviewer who thinks to compare the register's row set against the round sequence rather than to validate the rows present.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a register completeness clause to registerCoverageRule with the same GOVERNING status as its siblings: when authoring version N, predecessorVerdictFindings MUST contain an entry for every round from v6 through N-1 with no gaps, and each such entry MUST contain both the claude2 and codex lanes; a missing round or a missing lane REFUSES the successor. Because the round sequence is derivable from the version number and the lower bound is already stated as v6, this is mechanically checkable in the same way the existing checks are.

advisories.title: v23 changes nothing outside the review-bookkeeping machinery, now the eleventh consecutive generation
advisories.observation: Partitioning the v22 to v23 leaf diff, zero substantive paths changed and nothing was removed anywhere. The authorization content, failClosed's six conjuncts, coveredActs and its class gates, the authorizationRecord schema and its 19-member mapping, effectCommit, outcomeVocabulary and joinBlockerDisposition, is unchanged, and BLK-1 through BLK-4 remain STILL-ROUTED. The artifact has grown from 71101 bytes at recorded v8 to 142899 bytes, with essentially all growth in the machinery governing its own review; the register and its rules now account for the large majority of that.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: An observation about where review effort has gone, not a defect. Every bookkeeping finding across these eleven generations has been real, including four of mine and nine of Codex's, and the substantive content was independently examined and found coherent at v16 and v19. Nothing has regressed. Recorded a third time because the trend is unambiguous and a coordinator weighing whether this candidate is converging on DR-105 and DR-114 should have the measurement.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: None required of this artifact. Offered for coordinator awareness only.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Both claimed repairs are complete and I verified them by execution rather than by reading: the fromVnCheck scope conflict I raised at v22 is resolved with an explicit v8-onward bound and a named v6/v7 exclusion, and Codex's provenance binding is delivered as roundLaneIdentity, which I tested by running his own countermodel plus four substitution probes of my construction, all of which now refuse while the control passes. The full corpus from v6 through v22 passes every stated check with zero failures. The finding comes from the method refinement I fixed after missing Codex's last one: for each constrained field, state the property actually pinned and ask what remains free. At field level that came up clean, so I applied the same question to the register's row set, and there every check quantifies over entries that exist while no clause requires an entry to exist per round or both lanes to be present. That is not theoretical for this artifact: measuring its own history, v12 and v13 each carried only v6 and v7, missing five rounds including BLOCKER-carrying ones, and the omission survived two generations until I raised it at v13. Everything built since operates inside entries that exist, so a recurrence would still go undetected. The live register is complete, which is why this is SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker, and one clause of the same form as its eight siblings closes it.
